rfi.title: Privacy Policy / Privacy Notice
rfi.text: Privacy Policy / Privacy Notice Required India DPDPA: Assessed against notice obligations (Sections 5, 6); ISO 27001: Evidence for privacy and protection of personal information (A.5.34). What to send Privacy notice (CH2.NOTICE.1, CH2.NOTICE.3, ISO.A5.34) language options (CH2.NOTICE.1) retrospective notice template (CH2.NOTICE.2) website/app screenshot (CH2.NOTICE.3) terms linked from consent flows (CH2.CONSENT.1) Consent forms (CH2.NOTICE.1, CH2.NOTICE.3, CH2.CONSENT.1) screenshots of every consent capture flow (CH2.CONSENT.1) language selector screenshot (CH2.CONSENT.1) dated live screenshots or screen recording (CH2.CONSENT.1) Data flow diagram legacy consent population (CH2.NOTICE.2) Notice dispatch log (CH2.NOTICE.2) Grievance mechanism records sample rights-request responses (CH2.NOTICE.3) Legal and contractual register (ISO.A5.34) Roles and responsibilities (ISO.A5.34) Data processing register (ISO.A5.34) Example Current privacy notice and screen captures showing where people receive it. Good looks like Include the notice version, covered services and publication or distribution dates. Period (auditor): ________ Sample size (auditor): ________ Why we ask: 19 checks across 5 controls CH2.NOTICE.1 Notice accompanying the consent request Design A notice is presented before or together with every consent request, not only linked from a site footer. Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.5(1) [repo says 'at or before collection'; the Act ties the notice to consent requests, not to data collected under a s.7 legitimate use] Design The notice itemises the personal data collected and states the specified purpose(s) and the goods, services or uses each purpose enables. Evidence hint: Privacy notice Source basis: DPDPA s.5(1)(i); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b) Design The notice gives a link (or describes another means) through which the data principal can withdraw consent and exercise her rights. Evidence hint: Privacy notice Source basis: DPDPA s.5(1)(ii); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(c)(i)-(ii) [extends the repo description, which names only data and purpose, to the statutory minimum content] Design The notice describes how the data principal can complain to the Data Protection Board of India. Evidence hint: Privacy notice Source basis: DPDPA s.5(1)(iii); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(c)(iii) [extends the repo description to the statutory minimum content] Design The notice can be read in English or, at the data principal's option, in a language listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution. Evidence hint: Privacy notice (language options) Source basis: DPDPA s.5(3). Number of languages required is not settled by the text CH2.NOTICE.2 Notice for previously collected data Design The organisation has identified the data principals whose personal data it processes on consent given before the Act's notice and consent provisions commenced. Evidence hint: Data flow diagram (legacy consent population) Source basis: DPDPA s.5(2), s.1(2). 'Commencement' is read per provision (s.1(2)), i.e. consents given before mid-May 2027 Design A retrospective notice template states the personal data held, the purposes it has been processed for, how to withdraw consent and exercise rights, and how to complain to the Board. Evidence hint: Privacy notice (retrospective notice template) Source basis: DPDPA s.5(2)(a)(i)-(iii) Operating Dispatch records (email, in-app or other channel) show the retrospective notice was sent to the identified data principals, with dates. Evidence hint: Notice dispatch log Source basis: DPDPA s.5(2)(a) ('as soon as reasonably practicable'); what counts as timely after commencement is untested CH2.NOTICE.3 Notice contains contact details of DPO or grievance officer Design Each consent request gives contact details of the DPO (if an SDF) or of a person authorised to respond to data principals exercising their rights. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Privacy notice Source basis: DPDPA s.6(3) [repo cites s.5(1); the contact-details duty sits in s.6(3), s.8(9) and Rules r.9]. 'DPO' is defined only for SDFs (s.2(l)); 'grievance officer' is not an Act term Design The business contact information of the DPO, or of a person who can answer data principals' questions about processing, is prominently published on the website or app. Evidence hint: Privacy notice (website/app screenshot) Source basis: DPDPA s.8(9); DPDP Rules 2025 r.9 Operating A sample of responses to rights requests in the period includes that business contact information. Evidence hint: Grievance mechanism records (sample rights-request responses) Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.9 CH2.CONSENT.1 Lawful basis for processing with free, specific, informed consent Design Every consent request requires a clear affirmative action by the data principal; consent is never inferred from silence, a pre-ticked box, inactivity or continued use of the service. Evidence hint: Consent forms (screenshots of every consent capture flow) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) Design Every consent request names the specified purpose(s) for which the personal data will be processed. Evidence hint: Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b)(ii) Design The data principal is offered the option to read the consent request in English or in a language listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution. Evidence hint: Consent forms (language selector screenshot) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(3) [repo cites s.6(1)-(2); the language duty sits in s.6(3)]. How many Eighth Schedule languages must be offered is not settled by the text. 'Clear and plain language' is not tested: it is not binary Design No consent request contains a term by which the data principal waives a right under the Act or agrees to processing that would breach the Act or another law. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Privacy notice (terms linked from consent flows) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(2) Operating Consent screens captured from the live web/app during the assessment period match the approved consent design (affirmative action, purpose stated, no pre-selected choices). Evidence hint: Consent forms (dated live screenshots or screen recording) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) ISO.A5.34 Privacy and protection of personal information Design A privacy or PII protection policy identifies the privacy laws and contractual terms that apply to the organisation's processing of personal data. Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Legal and contractual register Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.34 Design A person or role is responsible for privacy and PII protection (e.g. DPO or privacy lead). Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Roles and responsibilities Source basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.34 (guidance) Operating A current record of personal data processing (e.g. data inventory or processing register) exists for the ISMS scope. Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Data processing register Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.34; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.34 (guidance) DPDPA ISO 27001 Documents requested Evidence already mapped for 2 of 5 requirements Already received

rfi.title: Consent forms / consent collection screenshots
rfi.text: Consent forms / consent collection screenshots Required Assessed for consent validity, granularity, and withdrawal mechanism What to send Consent forms (CH2.CONSENT.1, CH2.CONSENT.2, CH2.CONSENT.3, CM.GRANULAR.1, CM.GRANULAR.2) screenshots of every consent capture flow (CH2.CONSENT.1) language selector screenshot (CH2.CONSENT.1) dated live screenshots or screen recording (CH2.CONSENT.1) side-by-side give/withdraw flows (CH2.CONSENT.3) recorded walkthrough (CM.GRANULAR.2) Privacy notice (CH2.CONSENT.2, CH2.CONSENT.3) terms linked from consent flows (CH2.CONSENT.1) Consent log extract (CM.GRANULAR.1) sample of data principals (CH2.CONSENT.2) Retention schedule withdrawal procedure (CH2.CONSENT.3) Vendor agreements (CH2.CONSENT.3) Withdrawal procedure (CH2.CONSENT.3) Withdrawal log sample (CH2.CONSENT.3) Processor instruction records (CH2.CONSENT.3) Consent log schema (CM.GRANULAR.1) Terms of service (CM.GRANULAR.2) Example Consent forms, collection screen captures and withdrawal workflow. Good looks like Include form versions, purposes displayed and how consent choices are recorded. Period (auditor): ________ Sample size (auditor): ________ Why we ask: 19 checks across 5 controls CH2.CONSENT.1 Lawful basis for processing with free, specific, informed consent Design Every consent request requires a clear affirmative action by the data principal; consent is never inferred from silence, a pre-ticked box, inactivity or continued use of the service. Evidence hint: Consent forms (screenshots of every consent capture flow) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) Design Every consent request names the specified purpose(s) for which the personal data will be processed. Evidence hint: Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b)(ii) Design The data principal is offered the option to read the consent request in English or in a language listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution. Evidence hint: Consent forms (language selector screenshot) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(3) [repo cites s.6(1)-(2); the language duty sits in s.6(3)]. How many Eighth Schedule languages must be offered is not settled by the text. 'Clear and plain language' is not tested: it is not binary Design No consent request contains a term by which the data principal waives a right under the Act or agrees to processing that would breach the Act or another law. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Privacy notice (terms linked from consent flows) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(2) Operating Consent screens captured from the live web/app during the assessment period match the approved consent design (affirmative action, purpose stated, no pre-selected choices). Evidence hint: Consent forms (dated live screenshots or screen recording) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) CH2.CONSENT.2 Itemised consent for multiple purposes Design Where one collection point serves more than one purpose, the consent request lists each purpose as a separate item rather than a single combined purpose. Evidence hint: Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) ('specific'); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b)(ii) [repo cites s.6(3), which concerns language and contact details]. Per-purpose consent is a reading of 'specific', not express text Design The accompanying notice gives an itemised description of the personal data processed for each listed purpose. Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Consent forms Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b)(i) Operating Sampled consent records store a consent status for each purpose separately, not one combined flag. Evidence hint: Consent log extract (sample of data principals) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1), s.6(10) CH2.CONSENT.3 Consent withdrawal mechanism Design The notice or consent flow tells the data principal how to withdraw consent (link or described means). Evidence hint: Privacy notice; Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.5(1)(ii); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(c)(i) Design Withdrawing consent takes no more steps, and uses no less accessible a channel, than giving it did (e.g. consent given in-app can be withdrawn in-app). Evidence hint: Consent forms (side-by-side give/withdraw flows) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(4) [repo cites s.6(6)-(7); the withdrawal right sits in s.6(4), s.6(7) concerns Consent Managers]; DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(c)(i) Design A documented procedure makes the organisation stop the processing that relied on a withdrawn consent within a defined period, unless processing without consent is required or authorised by law. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Retention schedule (withdrawal procedure) Source basis: DPDPA s.6(6) Design The withdrawal procedure requires the organisation to make its Data Processors stop processing that data principal's personal data. Evidence hint: Vendor agreements; Withdrawal procedure Source basis: DPDPA s.6(6) Operating For a sample of withdrawals in the period, records show processing stopped (including at processors) within the defined period. Evidence hint: Withdrawal log sample; Processor instruction records Source basis: DPDPA s.6(6) ('within a reasonable time') CM.GRANULAR.1 Granular consent options available Design The consent interface provides a separate unticked control for each optional purpose. Evidence hint: Consent forms Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) ('specific'); DPDP Rules 2025 r.3(b)(ii) [repo cites s.6(3), which concerns language and contact details]. Largely overlaps CH2.CONSENT.2 Design Refusing or withdrawing one optional purpose leaves consent for the other purposes unchanged. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Consent log schema Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1), s.6(4) Operating Consent records contain data principals with mixed per-purpose states, showing partial consent works in practice. Evidence hint: Consent log extract Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) CM.GRANULAR.2 No consent bundling with service access Design Access to the service is not made conditional on consent to processing that the service does not need. Evidence hint: Consent forms; Terms of service Source basis: DPDPA s.6(1) ('unconditional'; consent limited to data necessary for the purpose, see the s.6(1) illustration) Design Consent screens show the accept and decline options with equal prominence. Evidence hint: Consent forms Source basis: practice ('dark patterns' is not a DPDPA term; pre-selection also fails s.6(1) 'clear affirmative action') Operating A test sign-up that declines every optional purpose completes and reaches the core service. rfi.title: Data retention schedule / policy
rfi.text: Data retention schedule / policy Required Assessed for storage limitation and deletion procedures What to send Retention schedule (CH2.MINIMIZE.2, CH2.MINIMIZE.3) Vendor agreements (CH2.MINIMIZE.2) Erasure warning template (CH2.MINIMIZE.2) Deletion job logs / erasure records sample (CH2.MINIMIZE.2) System configuration screenshots (CH2.MINIMIZE.3) Example Retention schedule, deletion procedure and completed deletion records. Good looks like Identify data categories, retention triggers, owners and deletion dates. Period (auditor): ________ Sample size (auditor): ________ Why we ask: 9 checks across 2 controls CH2.MINIMIZE.2 Data retention limited to purpose fulfilment Design The retention procedure requires erasure when consent is withdrawn or when it is reasonable to assume the specified purpose is no longer served, whichever comes first, unless a named law requires retention. Evidence hint: Retention schedule Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7)(a) Design The procedure requires Data Processors to erase personal data the organisation made available to them when erasure is triggered. Evidence hint: Retention schedule; Vendor agreements Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7)(b) Design If the organisation is an e-commerce entity or social media intermediary with at least 2 crore registered users in India, or an online gaming intermediary with at least 50 lakh, the procedure erases a user's data after three years without her approaching it or exercising rights (excluding account and virtual-token access). Evidence hint: Retention schedule Source basis: DPDPA s.8(8); DPDP Rules 2025 r.8(1), Third Schedule Design For organisations in the Third Schedule classes, the procedure warns the data principal at least 48 hours before inactivity-based erasure. Evidence hint: Retention schedule; Erasure warning template Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.8(2) Operating Erasure job logs or erasure records for the period show personal data past its erasure trigger was actually erased. Evidence hint: Retention schedule; Deletion job logs / erasure records sample Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7) CH2.MINIMIZE.3 Retention schedule and deletion procedures Design A retention schedule sets a retention period or erasure trigger for each personal data category or processing purpose. Evidence hint: Retention schedule Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7); the schedule document itself is practice Design Where the schedule keeps data after its purpose is served, it names the law that requires the retention. Evidence hint: Retention schedule Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7) Design No schedule period erases personal data, associated traffic data or processing logs sooner than one year after the processing, unless another law requires otherwise. Evidence hint: Retention schedule Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.8(3), Seventh Schedule Operating Retention or deletion settings on a sample of systems holding personal data match the schedule's periods. Evidence hint: Retention schedule; System configuration screenshots Source basis: DPDPA s.8(7) DPDPA Documents requested Evidence already mapped for 0 of 2 requirements Already received

rfi.title: Breach notification procedure / incident response plan
rfi.text: Breach notification procedure / incident response plan Required India DPDPA: Assessed against breach intimation obligations (Section 8(6); DPDP Rules 2025 r.7); ISO 27001: Evidence for incident planning, assessment, response, learning and evidence collection (A.5.24-A.5.28), contact with authorities (A.5.5) and event reporting (A.6.8). What to send Incident and breach procedure (BN.NOTIFY.1, BN.NOTIFY.2, BN.NOTIFY.3, ISO.A5.24, ISO.A5.26, ISO.A5.27, ISO.A5.5, ISO.A6.8) Board report template (BN.NOTIFY.1) notification template (BN.NOTIFY.2) exercise records (ISO.A5.24) classification and severity matrix (ISO.A5.25) evidence handling section (ISO.A5.28) authority contact list (ISO.A5.5) contact list review date (ISO.A5.5) Incident log (BN.NOTIFY.1, BN.NOTIFY.2, BN.NOTIFY.3, ISO.A5.26, ISO.A6.8) event triage records (ISO.A5.25) post-incident reviews (ISO.A5.27) evidence records (ISO.A5.28) Board submission records (BN.NOTIFY.1) Notification dispatch records (BN.NOTIFY.2) Exercise report (BN.NOTIFY.3) Roles and responsibilities (ISO.A5.24) Training records (ISO.A5.24) awareness content (ISO.A6.8) Legal and contractual register (ISO.A5.26) Change management or risk assessment updates (ISO.A5.27) Information security policy (ISO.A6.8) Example Incident response plan, escalation contacts and notification workflow. Good looks like Include the current version, owner and records of any exercises or use. Period (auditor): ________ Sample size (auditor): ________ Why we ask: 31 checks across 10 controls BN.NOTIFY.1 Breach notification to Data Protection Board Design The breach procedure requires an initial intimation to the Data Protection Board without delay on becoming aware of a personal data breach, describing its nature, extent, timing, location and likely impact. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDPA s.8(6); DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(2)(a) Design The procedure requires a detailed follow-up report to the Board within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, or within a longer period the Board allows on a written request. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(2)(b) [the 72-hour period comes from the Rules; Act s.8(6) sets no timeline] Design The Board report template covers updated details of the breach, its facts and causes, mitigation measures, findings on who caused it, measures to prevent recurrence, and a report of the intimations sent to data principals. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (Board report template) Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(2)(b)(i)-(vi) Design The procedure applies to every personal data breach as defined in the Act, with no harm or materiality threshold for intimating the Board. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDPA s.2(u), s.8(6) Operating For each personal data breach in the period, records show the initial intimation and the detailed report reached the Board on time. Evidence hint: Incident log; Board submission records Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(2) BN.NOTIFY.2 Breach notification to affected Data Principals Design The breach procedure requires intimating each affected data principal without delay, through her user account or a communication channel she registered. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDPA s.8(6); DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(1) Design The data principal notification template covers the breach's nature, extent and timing; likely consequences for her; mitigation measures taken; steps she can take; and a contact for queries. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (notification template) Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(1)(a)-(e) Design The procedure notifies every affected data principal, with no risk or harm threshold. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDPA s.8(6); DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(1) Operating For each personal data breach in the period, records show affected data principals were sent a notification containing the template content. Evidence hint: Incident log; Notification dispatch records Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(1) BN.NOTIFY.3 Incident response plan documented Design An approved incident response plan covers detection, containment, investigation, notification and remediation of personal data breaches. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: practice (supports DPDPA s.8(5); DPDP Rules 2025 r.6(1)(c), r.7) Design The plan names the roles that decide a breach has occurred and that send the Board and data principal intimations. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: practice (supports DPDP Rules 2025 r.7) Design The plan includes a method for identifying affected data principals and their registered contact channels. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: DPDP Rules 2025 r.7(1) (needed to notify each affected data principal) Operating The plan was exercised (tabletop or real incident) in the last 12 months and lessons were recorded. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure; Incident log; Exercise report Source basis: practice ISO.A5.24 Information security incident management planning and preparation Design A documented incident management procedure covers detection, reporting, triage, response, communication and closure. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.24 Design Incident management roles (e.g. incident manager, response team, communications lead) are defined with named people and contact details. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure; Roles and responsibilities Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.24 Operating The incident procedure and roles were communicated to those involved, and the plan was exercised (e.g. tabletop) in the last 12 months. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (exercise records); Training records Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.24 ('communicating'); exercising is ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.24 (guidance) ISO.A5.25 Assessment and decision on information security events Design Written criteria define when a security event is classified as an incident, with severity or priority levels. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (classification and severity matrix) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.25 Operating For a sample of logged events, the record shows an assessment and a decision on whether each was an incident. Evidence hint: Incident log (event triage records) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.25 ISO.A5.26 Response to information security incidents Design Response procedures cover containment, eradication, recovery, escalation and notification to internal and external parties. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.26; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.26 (guidance) Operating For a sample of incidents in the period, the incident record shows the documented steps were followed and the incident was closed. Evidence hint: Incident log Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.26 Operating Where an incident triggered a legal or contractual notification duty, the record shows notification was made within the required time. Evidence hint: Incident log; Incident and breach procedure; Legal and contractual register Source basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.26 (guidance); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.31 ISO.A5.27 Learning from information security incidents Design The incident procedure requires a post-incident review for significant incidents. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.27; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.27 (guidance) Operating For significant incidents in the period, a post-incident review was recorded and at least one resulting control improvement was tracked to completion. Evidence hint: Incident log (post-incident reviews); Change management or risk assessment updates Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.27 ISO.A5.28 Collection of evidence Design A procedure covers identifying, collecting, acquiring and preserving evidence of security events, including chain of custody. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (evidence handling section) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.28 Operating Where evidence was collected in the period, a chain-of-custody or evidence-handling record exists. Evidence hint: Incident log (evidence records) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.28; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.28 (guidance) ISO.A5.5 Contact with authorities Design A current contact list names the authorities to contact (e.g. data protection regulator, CERT-In or national CERT, law enforcement, sector regulator) and when. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (authority contact list) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.5 Design The incident procedure states who is authorised to contact authorities and within what timelines for reportable events. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure Source basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.5 (guidance) Operating The authority contact list has been verified or updated within the last 12 months. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure (contact list review date) Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.5 ('maintained') ISO.A6.8 Information security event reporting Design A reporting channel for security events (e.g. email alias, portal, hotline) is defined and published to personnel. Evidence hint: Incident and breach procedure; Information security policy Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.8 Operating The incident log contains events reported by personnel through the channel in the period, with timestamps showing timely reporting. Evidence hint: Incident log Source basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.8 Operating Awareness material tells personnel what to report and how. rfi.title: Grievance redressal mechanism documentation
rfi.text: Grievance redressal mechanism documentation Required Must demonstrate accessible grievance channel with named officer What to send Grievance mechanism records (CH3.GRIEVANCE.1, CH3.GRIEVANCE.2) grievance log (CH3.GRIEVANCE.1) grievance log with receipt and response dates (CH3.GRIEVANCE.2) response template (CH3.GRIEVANCE.2) Privacy notice (CH3.GRIEVANCE.1) DPO appointment record (CH3.GRIEVANCE.1) Example Grievance procedure, contact page and case register.
